# Guild routing

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-skill-docs.py from docs/reference/skills.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

For what each skill reads and writes, see the [skills reference](reference/skills.md). This file maps each `/crav1-…` skill and `*-agent` subagent to a lane — Specify, Plan, Build, or Cross-cutting — and records cross-cutting helpers, so a kit consumer can route work when the kit changes. Cross-cutting skills may be invoked from any phase, and cross-cutting helpers may be flagged from any phase. Neither is owned by Specify, Plan, or Build alone, and neither by itself moves work into another lane.

Kit source of truth: [https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit](https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit).

Skill slash names are `/crav1-…`. Subagent names end in `-agent`.

## Starter options

When the user asks for startup options, these six are the only ways in. That ask names the list. It does not run a skill. It does not move work into a lane. Each starter still follows the rules it already has. Every other skill is a later skill.

| Starter | Runs when |
| --- | --- |
| `/crav1-spark-to-spec` | The user brings one or two sentences |
| `/crav1-ideas-to-spec` | The user brings a pile of ideas and technical hunches |
| `/crav1-bundle-to-specs` | The user brings mixed files, or more than one v0 feature |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | The user names existing repos, with or without a dump to match |
| `/crav1-read-environment` | The user names the host |
| `/crav1-fix-bug` | The user names a real bug |

The same list is where a lone user sees the ways to start: [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md) and [first-run.md](first-run.md).

`/crav1-tighten-spec` reads `spec.md`, diagrams, ADRs, reviewer findings already in the chat, and, when the slice is partial or `## In the code` names paths, the committed code on the repo and branch that spec names. It writes only the picked issue in `spec.md` and, when that pick says so, the named diagram, ADR, or export. It writes a branch onto the spec only after a yes. It leaves application code and unpicked issues alone. A spec with no code behind it skips that read. The user calls it. It calls no skill.

Exception: a different open repo or branch, a missing branch, a stub, or a spec too thin for that read stops and does not tighten. `suggest` does not patch. A disagreement with the code is called out and the spec is not rewritten to match the code. Finish, add a test, and leave are not choices here. A stale research mark may be one issue. It does not clear the mark.

`/crav1-add-to-spec`, `/crav1-bundle-to-specs`, and `/crav1-existing-to-specs` follow the imported-sources check when they quote an imported source. That check recommends keep or redact for personal data. Items it cannot place are asked in one batch. Secrets are always redacted and are never a choice. The check may write the transfer data policy after a yes. Cursor: `.cursor/rules/crav1-transfer-data-policy.mdc`. Claude Code project: `.claude/rules/crav1-transfer-data-policy.md`. It never writes a secrets choice into that file. For a mail, it lists each embedded image, inline or attached. It recommends convert to text when the image is a diagram, a table, or text that can be reproduced exactly, and compress otherwise. It asks once before the source folder is written. Auto-accept applies to those recommendations only when the transfer data policy clearly covers them. The user changes the rule by editing or deleting the file. `/crav1-add-to-spec` write `docs/notes/` when the user picks Note. A note keeps the quote without tying it to a spec yet. There is no question after Note about what kind of note it is. They read `docs/notes/` first. An item already noted is not written again. `/crav1-add-to-spec` writes `Used by <slug>` when a spec quotes a note, and `Absorbed by <slug>` only after the user says yes and one spec takes the whole note. Status stays open until then. `/crav1-spark-to-spec`, `/crav1-ideas-to-spec`, `/crav1-bundle-to-specs`, `/crav1-existing-to-specs`, and `/crav1-tighten-spec` do the same when they quote a note. They do not commit.

After a quote is kept, `/crav1-add-to-spec` also compares it with notes in `docs/research/` and with `## Research findings` on the specs it touches, including notes those findings link to. `/crav1-add-to-spec` does that through its fact branch and does not run the check a second time. A clear contradiction of a research line, and a quote that answers an open question in the note or the findings, are both listed. The new quote is shown next to the research line or the question. An unclear case is not marked. It stays an open question on the spec. The research is marked only after the user says yes. The note gets a blockquote below the title and the owner line. The note's own text is not changed. The spec's Research findings get a `Stale since` line that sees the note. The kit may then draft a short revisit request in the chat for the note's owner, taken from the note. It drafts only. It does not send the request or contact anyone. When the note names no owner, it says so and drafts without one. The question asks the owner to say, per point, resolved, partly, or not addressed, and why when it is still open. The status line says the kit checks the updated note against each listed point when it comes back to `docs/research/`. When an updated note is written to `docs/research/`, or the user replaces the file and points `/crav1-add-to-spec` or `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` at it, the kit checks each listed point from the update's text. It does not ask the user. An older mark with no point lines is not one point. It is split into the contradiction and answered-question hits named in the note's stale block, the spec's stale line, and the run that wrote them when that run is visible. Each hit is judged. When those hits cannot be found, the whole update is judged against the original quote, and the summary says the older mark had no points. The mark clears when that quote is resolved, and it is left as written when it is not. When the mark has listed points, every point resolved removes the stale block and the spec line, and records a `Cleared` line with one short line per point. Otherwise that mark stays and is narrowed to how many points are still open. Resolved points are recorded with the update that resolved them. Each open point is routed from the owner's reason. Research that missed it or got it wrong gets a follow-up revisit draft for the note's owner, for those points only. A fact someone else has, or a decision, becomes an open question on the spec and is not sent back to the owner. When the update does not say why, the kit asks the owner once who can answer it. The updated note's own open questions are read too. A question whose answer lies outside the note's owner is written on each spec whose Research findings link to that note. The question names who has the fact when the note says so. A decision is marked as a decision. A question the note's owner can still answer stays in the note. The same meaning already on the spec is not written again. This still runs when the mark clears. The summary lists every one of those questions. A spec line the update says to change becomes an open question. The question names the note's owner's revisit answer, with its date, or the note's section when the wording is in the note. It uses the owner's name when the note or the answer names them. It does not attribute to the note what is only in the answer. The spec line stays. `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` re-checks a point when the open question it was waiting on is answered, and clears the mark when no point is open. A new source through the impact check does the same. The kit drafts only. It does not send anything. It does not commit. The shared wording is [`.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/research-stale.md`](../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/research-stale.md). These skills do not commit.

## Plan

| Kind | Name |
| --- | --- |
| Skill | `/crav1-plan-from-spec` |
| Skill | `/crav1-review-plan` |
| Skill | `/crav1-tighten-plan` |

`/crav1-plan-from-spec` reads the accepted spec, diagrams, ADRs, exports, kept security findings already written, and, when the spec is partial or `## In the code` names paths, that same committed repo and branch before any task is written. It writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md`, and matching OpenSpec export files when those already exist. A built piece that already matches v0 is marked already there and gets no rebuild task. A piece the user leaves gets one line in the plan and no task. It lists stale research findings under Risks. That does not block the plan. It leaves `spec.md`, application code, and any linter install alone. The user calls it. It calls no skill.

Exception: when `## Linter` says this repo has no linter for the code the tasks will touch, it stops before Build until the user chooses. A line under `## Dismissed test suggestions` is not a task. A kept test suggestion that is already an acceptance line maps to a task. A gap or a disagreement is finish, add a verify test, or leave before any task exists. A later run does not turn a left piece into work unless the user says so.

`/crav1-review-plan` reads `spec.md`, `plan.md`, and `tasks.md`. It writes nothing. It leaves the plan and code alone. The user calls it. It calls no skill.

Exception: the parent delegates the critique and does not review in its own voice. It names `/crav1-tighten-plan` and does not run it. A piece marked already there or left as committed is not a missing task.

`/crav1-existing-to-specs` is a starter option. Asking for startup options names it and does not run it. It may run from any lane. The user names one or more repos. It still runs only when the user names repos. It reads those repos and writes one architecture spec the lanes can extend (`docs/architecture/spec.md`) when that file is missing, and the system notes in `docs/system/` that `/crav1-explain-existing-system` reads when those notes are missing. When a real system note is already there, it leaves those notes except the `Synced at` line in `repos.md` of a repo it read, and writes the missing architecture spec and `docs/architecture/left-out.md`. When the architecture spec or those notes are already there, a later re-read adds only what is new and does not rewrite lines that are already there, except that `Synced at` line in `repos.md`. A fact the code shows is confirmed. Before any file is written, the confirmation stays in sections: one per named repo for confirmed facts, one for inferred guesses, one for links, and one for left-out. Each section has its own question and its own answer. Every item stays listed. A guess stays out until that section’s answer accepts it, and then it is accepted from a guess, not a code fact. Confirming a guess does not turn it into a link. A guess that stays left out is written to `docs/architecture/left-out.md`, beside the architecture spec. That file stays in `docs/architecture/`. A later re-read reads it and checks the code for every line. When the code shows the fact or a real link, the line comes off that file and is written as a fact or a link. When the code still does not show it, the line stays. The left-out answer can accept a line, keep it left out, or dismiss it. Dismiss means it is not offered again. A link is written only when the code shows it. If none is found, that section says so and does not offer a guessed link. It does not invent links. It does not design the next feature, write application code, or start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not `/crav1-add-to-spec`. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-existing-to-specs recheck` (also `repos vs specs`, since 1.108.0) may run from any lane once specs exist. It compares the named repos, or every repo in `docs/system/repos.md`, with the existing specs, optionally narrowed to a path or to code changed since the last read. It reports code no spec covers and stale claims (cited paths that are gone), refreshes `## Code with no slice` in `docs/system/landscape.md`, and writes nothing into any spec and never an open question. A gap goes to `/crav1-add-to-spec` only after a yes; a new feature is named, not started.

`/crav1-read-environment` is a starter option. Asking for startup options names it and does not run it. It may run from any lane. The user names the host at the start. It still runs only when the user names the host. Examples: Azure, AWS, Google Cloud. Naming production, prod, or live stops. It does not guess the host. It never reads production data. One pass reads every non-prod environment. Each seen line keeps its own environment. A prod-only line says `Seen in <host> prod.` and `prod only`. Each host has its own reader. A host with no reader stops and says so. It does not pretend to read it. This build has readers for Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. Any other named host stops with no reader. It does not read Azure DevOps, GitHub, or CI. The user names the host, not the subscription, the account, or the project. Marks come from the name, the group, the tags, and `docs/environments/marks.md` when that file exists. Non-prod tokens are dev, development, test, testing, stage, staging, uat, and qa. Pre-prod, a resource marked both non-prod and production by different sources, and a prod-only resource are shape and connections only, after one yes. The mixed resource is labelled `shared with prod`. Prod-only means the only mark is production, so there is no non-prod twin on that resource. A no lists them as not read. A declined prod-only resource stays skipped. Look-inside never opens production. An unmarked resource can be marked from shown evidence, strongest first. What is still unmarked is asked, then left unread, marked by the user, or stops the read. The skill appends only confirmed lines to `docs/environments/marks.md`. It does not write `docs/system`, `docs/architecture/spec.md`, a feature spec, or `docs/architecture/left-out.md`. A fact is marked seen in that environment, not as something the code shows. A link, including a trigger definition, is added only when the environment shows the connection. After the first read, and before any section, it can look inside a database or storage when the user says yes. SQL is metadata only. Storage is structure only, prefix depth 2. It never reads a row or a blob, and it never reports a file count or a size. Production is never opened. When the databases have no clear environment, it says there are no clear database environments and asks, options only, one question at a time. It does not install a tool, and it does not create a login, a firewall rule, a role, or a key. Missing access stops that look-inside and names the gap. Facts still say seen in that environment and join the sections that already exist. If the CLI or the login is missing, the stop names which. The skill does not install a CLI and does not log in. Confirmation is one section at a time, with its own question and answer, and nothing is dropped to keep a section short. After the user confirms a section, the skill that already owns the file adds only what is new. System facts go to `docs/system` through `/crav1-refresh-system-notes`. Architecture facts go to `docs/architecture/spec.md` through `/crav1-existing-to-specs`. A slice Match already owns goes on that feature spec through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. A left-out line the environment now shows comes off `docs/architecture/left-out.md` through `/crav1-existing-to-specs`. Lines that are already there are not rewritten. It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. After `docs/environments/marks.md` lines are added, it asks once whether to run `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` and does not run that refresh from the question.

`/crav1-fix-bug` may run from any lane, and only when the user names a real bug in that turn. A real bug is a verify failure on work that is already shipping, or a defect that comes in from outside. If they have not named one, it stops. It does not go hunting. It names the lane and does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start that lane. A spec miss goes to Specify. A plan miss goes to Plan. A verify miss or a broken implementation goes to Build. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it. It is not a stretch of verify. When the user asks for startup options, this skill is one of the six starter options above. That ask names the list and does not run this skill. It is an intake for a bug that already exists. It still runs only when the user names a real bug. It is not a skill that runs because a repo is new, and it is not started automatically. When the bug changes how the parts connect, it asks once whether to run `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` and does not run it.

`/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` may run from any lane. The user names a person, one spec, a topic, a branch, or a pull request. It gathers the open questions for that selection, including questions routed via that person. Pending questions from an earlier run are shown first. It drafts a mail, a meeting agenda, a chat message, or meeting questions to ask out loud. Meeting questions lists every selected question. The draft is numbered and grouped by topic in plain words, in English or the language named, and never names a spec slug, a path, or a question id. The personal-data and secrets check runs on the draft. Nothing is sent. After the draft it asks yes, no, or pending. Yes writes an asked mark under each question. No writes nothing. Pending writes a pending mark. `/crav1-add-to-spec` link answers back and take the asked-on date from the source, following [`.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/open-questions.md`](../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/open-questions.md). It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-add-to-spec` may run from any lane. Everything after the command, and every `@`, is the input. An email or a chat thread is accepted as well as minutes or a transcript. If there is no pointer, it stops and asks. Options only. It does not guess. The kind is `meeting`, `email`, or `chat`, from what the input shows. If the kind is not clear, it asks once per run, options only. The date comes from the input. It does not invent one. When the input shows no date, it asks once per run, options only: give a date, or skip. One kind and one date apply to every item. It extracts requirements, decisions, changes, open questions, and bugs as quotes, with speaker and time when the input shows them, and drops small talk. It matches each item to existing `docs/specs/<slug>/` folders, skipping `_template`. Cases are an addition, a possible new feature, a bug, or unclear. When more than one existing spec could fit, every candidate stays listed. Nothing is dropped to keep the list short. Each item that matches an existing spec shows one line, `State: <state>.`, and a short reason that names the evidence, in the item block and in the question. The states are built, partly built, planned, and not built. `Fits: none` has no state line. Evidence is that slice’s `spec.md` (including `## Match`), `plan.md`, `tasks.md` checkboxes, and `verify.md` when present. When those do not settle it, one read-only look at the code that spec or plan points to. A code-based or uncertain state is labeled `(inference, not in the docs)`. The line does not change keep, leave, or dismiss. It is not written and it is not passed to `/crav1-add-to-spec` as quote text. The user answers the items in one batch: keep, leave, or dismiss. Since 1.61.0 every input (fact, dump, code change, meeting) is saved once as one full note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` by source date, with generated indexes; each spec gets its short points with a `Full source:` link, and notes are never absorbed. Leave keeps nothing extra; the item stays in the full note. The recommendation is Leave when no spec fits. This skill asks every item in one batch; a single yes takes the recommendations. It checks the notes indexes first: the same source again is `already imported on <date> as <note>`, reuse or skip, never a second copy. The same point from another source becomes a second source on the spec line; a disagreement is flagged as a conflict. Dismiss is for this run only, and for a greeting, scheduling, and thanks. The next run starts fresh. It does not write a dismissals file. A kept addition is handed to `/crav1-add-to-spec` for that slug. The handoff passes the kind, the date, and the source folder when one was written. The quote starts with `From <kind> <date>.` when there is a date, otherwise `From <kind>.` The impact check still runs there, including research, in that handoff. This skill does not run the research check a second time. A kept new feature names `/crav1-spark-to-spec`, `/crav1-ideas-to-spec`, or `/crav1-bundle-to-specs` and does not run it. A kept bug names `/crav1-fix-bug` and does not run it. When a kept addition imports a source, it writes `docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/` following the imported-sources convention and does not write the spec. That check may write the transfer data policy after a yes. Cursor: `.cursor/rules/crav1-transfer-data-policy.mdc`. Claude Code project: `.claude/rules/crav1-transfer-data-policy.md`. It never writes a secrets choice into that file. For a mail, it lists each embedded image, inline or attached. It recommends convert to text when the image is a diagram, a table, or text that can be reproduced exactly, and compress otherwise. It asks once before the source folder is written. Auto-accept applies to those recommendations only when the transfer data policy clearly covers them. The user changes the rule by editing or deleting the file. It does not commit. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start those lanes. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. The six starter options stay unchanged. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it. It reads spec open questions first. A clear answer is linked under the question without a keep question. An unclear or partial answer is shown and the question stays open. A question the input shows being asked gets that date as its asked-on date.

`/crav1-review-pr` may run from any lane, and only when the user names an open pull request (number or URL) in that turn, or clearly asks to review that pull request. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It only names the lane for a finding. A pull request with no `plan.md` or `tasks.md` for its slug was built outside the kit. That is an info note, not a fix finding. It does not report a missing `verify.md`. It reads the test results that pull request's own pipeline already recorded and does not run tests. It names `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` after that pull request merges and does not run it. A pull request that has a plan keeps the plan and `verify.md` checks. Spark, specify, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-pr-status` may run from any lane, and only when the user names a pull request (number or URL) in that turn, or the current branch has exactly one open pull request. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It reads the threads read-only, writes the PR note's shared PR record, drafts replies and never posts them, and changes a thread's status on the host only on that thread's own yes (1.97.0). It hands spec or decision points to `/crav1-add-to-spec` on a yes and follow-ups to `/crav1-ado-sync` as drafts.

`/crav1-merge-pr` may run from any lane, and only when the user explicitly asks in that turn to merge a named pull request. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-help` may run from any lane. It answers what to run next, in what order, and what a skill does, from the kit's own docs (the kit repo's `docs/`, or the `crav1-docs/` folder bundled next to the skills in every install), never GitHub. The order comes from the routes in `docs/reference/workflow.yaml`. Every answer names its source. It writes nothing and runs no skill. `todo` ranks what to do next from the records, scoped by person, spec, topic, branch, or pull request as [`.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/scope.md`](../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/scope.md) says. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option. Agents call it before they suggest more than one next step, as `crav1.mdc` says.

`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` may run from any lane, any time, when you type it. It is command-only (1.88.0). It lists which tasks are ready to build and why the others are blocked, from `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `verify.md`. It never reads Azure Boards. It writes nothing and runs no skill. It names `/crav1-build-tasks` and does not run it. It does not move work into Build. It is not a starter option.

`/crav1-explain-existing-system` may run from any lane. It reads the system notes already in `docs/system/`. The first answer is a short TLDR. Longer goes one level deeper from the same notes. It stays read-only. It shows a stale research note as stale. It does not clear the mark. On every run it compares the feature index with each slice's node in `docs/system/diagrams.md` and its line in `## How the parts connect`. Names match only by slug, spec title, or main resource name. It lists each slice missing entirely or partly, including done and retired, with status, and names `/crav1-refresh-system-notes`. It does not run it. When the picture has nothing on the question, it quotes the first paragraph of the matching spec, labelled as coming from the spec, and names `/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this`. When no spec matches either, it says so and names that skill. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not write a file.

`/crav1-explain-this-code` may run from any lane, any time, on its own. The user names a file, a function, a selection, or a pull request diff; when none is named it asks what to explain. It opens with one question with choice words: `what it does` (Recommended), `what and why`, or `teach the language`, and skips it when the wording answers. A headless or bot run with no word stops and lists the words. It reads only the code and the code it calls and never guesses. Reasons come only from the code, specs, plan decisions, system notes, and commits, else `no stated reason found`. Every answer has a small mermaid flowchart built from what was read. It is read-only and explains in chat. It writes nothing to `docs/` or the kit layout. At the end it offers Save as .md: after showing the full path and asking, it writes to the user's Downloads folder or a path the user names, never into the repo by default. The kit never reads that file. It is not `/crav1-explain-existing-system`. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-retire-spec` may run from any lane, any time, on its own, on one spec the user names. It opens with one question with choice words: `retire` (Recommended), `merge`, `park`, or `convert to note`, and skips it when the wording answers. A headless or bot run with no word stops and lists the words. It shows a summary of every change and writes only after a yes. It never deletes; a moved spec leaves a `Moved:` pointer. Retire and merge move the spec to `docs/specs/retired/`, which every spec-scanning skill skips. Merge suggests only real fits with a reason, or says `no good merge fit found`. Park leaves the spec in place with a `Parked:` line; `/crav1-plan-from-spec`, `/crav1-build-tasks`, `/crav1-build-features`, and the push branches of `/crav1-ado-sync` skip it, and `/crav1-add-to-spec` saves matching input as one note waiting for it. Convert to note writes `docs/notes/` and one landscape line. It runs no other skill. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build.

`/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this` may run from any lane. The user asks about one feature, slice, resource, or not-yet-feature. The answer comes from the specs first. It reads only. It writes nothing. It shows a stale research note as stale. It does not clear the mark. One pass matches an exact name first, then key words, with spec titles and Match quotes weighted highest. One winning slice is the answer, and the path is named. Two or more close hits are listed and it asks which. It does not guess. No slice: it says so and presents a candidate slice. It names `/crav1-spark-to-spec`, `/crav1-ideas-to-spec`, or `/crav1-bundle-to-specs` and does not run them. Pasted minutes or a long dump names `/crav1-add-to-spec` and stops. After the repo part it runs read-only Azure and Azure DevOps checks. Production is shape and connections only, after the same yes or no as `/crav1-read-environment`. It never reads data. A failed live read offers Retry or Skip. It may name one skill. It does not run another skill. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start those lanes. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. The six starter options stay unchanged. It is not `/crav1-explain-existing-system`. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-refresh-system-notes` may run from any lane, on its own. When the user points it at an updated note in `docs/research/`, it checks each listed point on a stale mark. It clears, narrows, or routes that point. An older mark with no point lines is split into the hits it was made from. It also routes the note's own open questions when the answer lies outside the note's owner, including when the mark clears. It does not ask the user. It does not commit. The passes that already append a glossary row also run this picture update. Spark, ideas, intake, match, match-dump, add-to-spec, and existing-to-specs update the picture in their own pass. It adds what is new to the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect. When this run reads a whole repo, it sets that repo's `Synced at` line in `repos.md` and touches only those repos. When this run reads only one slice, it leaves the `repos.md` section alone and writes the slice line. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not design the change and does not build it. `/crav1-build-features` asks when a slice is marked done or retired. `/crav1-fix-bug` and `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` ask when the fix changes how the parts connect. `/crav1-read-environment` asks after marks lines are added. `/crav1-add-to-spec` asks once at the end of a read-environment or suggest-tests handoff. Those asks do not run this command. `/crav1-build-tasks` do not ask.

`/crav1-map-pipeline-environments` may run from any lane. The user names Azure DevOps, the org, and the project. A pipeline name is optional. If any of those three is missing, it stops and asks. Options only. It does not guess. It reads pipeline definitions with `az pipelines` and `az devops` and does not run a pipeline. The stage name gives the environment, with the same whole-word rule as `/crav1-read-environment`. It appends only confirmed lines to `docs/environments/marks.md`. It does not write `docs/system`, `docs/architecture/spec.md`, a feature spec, or `docs/architecture/left-out.md`. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start those lanes. It names `/crav1-read-environment` and does not run it. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. The six starter options stay unchanged. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-review-security` may run from any lane, and only after architecture already exists (`docs/system/` or a spec that already describes the design). The same command reviews the whole system, one existing spec, or the change in front of us. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. Spark, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-glossary` may run from any lane (1.101.0). With no word it shows `docs/system/glossary.md` in the chat in file order and writes nothing. `research` fills the `to be researched` rows: a meaning stated in `docs/` is written with a file and line link without asking; a public term may be searched on the web after the personal-data check, and that meaning is written only after a yes; an internal-only term never goes to the web. `<term>` answers one word and offers to add a missing row on a yes. A term found nowhere gets a labelled guess with Correct or Needs research; it never writes an open question onto a spec (1.105.0). It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build, and it does not commit.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Suggest Features) may run from any lane. It reads the landscape, the specs, research, sources, and every note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` (notes are never absorbed since 1.61.0). A stale research note is shown as stale. A fact from a note is labelled as a note. A note is not a candidate by itself. It lists Feature candidates. A dated milestone or slice is one candidate. An undated spec with open work is one candidate. A spec that holds only open questions is marked questions only. An item with no spec is marked no spec yet. It skips a spec that is done or retired with nothing open. It shows a recorded Azure Boards id. It gives a target date only when the docs state it. It writes nothing unless the user asks for a file. It does not call Azure Boards. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start those lanes. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. The six starter options stay unchanged. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it. `/crav1-ado-sync` runs it.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Push Features) may run from any lane. It takes the Azure DevOps org and project from `docs/environments/marks.md` or from the Azure DevOps URLs in `docs/system/repos.md`. It checks `az`, including the default install paths, and that the project has the Feature work item type. Before the preview it reads the Feature fields. When that type has Acceptance Criteria, the checks go there. When it does not, the checks go in the Description as an Acceptance checks list, that field is not sent, and the preview says so. A failed field read states the issue, suggests a fix, and offers a skip. It does not guess. It runs `/crav1-ado-sync` and the user picks by number or all. It previews the Feature form. It creates or updates a Feature only after the user says yes. The same field rule applies on an update. After a Create, writing the new id into that spec’s `work-item.md`, or a row on the landscape `## No spec yet in ADO` table when the item has no spec, is required. The closing output names that file, says it is not committed yet, names `/crav1-finalize-commit`, and says a later run would offer Create again. If the write fails, it prints the line to add. Nothing it sends mentions the specs repo. A preview edit goes into the spec through `/crav1-add-to-spec` first. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start those lanes. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. The six starter options stay unchanged. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it. At the end it names `/crav1-ado-sync` and does not run it.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Push tasks) may run from any lane. It uses the same `az` checks and the same org and project as `/crav1-ado-sync`. The user picks one spec that already has a Feature id in `work-item.md`. It lists every task in that spec's `tasks.md`, numbered, and the user picks by number or all. The child work item type is asked once and saved as a line in `docs/environments/marks.md`. It previews each task form (fuller title, State New, Iteration and Priority blank, tags, owner when stated, fuller description, the verify line as acceptance), strips paths, line numbers, spec references, and kit names while keeping code repo names, and creates or updates a child of the Feature only after the user says yes. It records `Work item: <id> — task: T<n> <short title>` in `work-item.md`, never in `tasks.md`. It names `/crav1-finalize-commit` and does not run it. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it. It names `/crav1-ado-sync` as the later read-back.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Pull tasks) may run from any lane. It uses the same `az` checks as `/crav1-ado-sync`. The user picks a spec with task lines in `work-item.md`, or all. It reads back every recorded task item (State, title, description, acceptance, Assigned To, comments, history) and shows only what differs from the spec and `tasks.md`, plus new children of the Feature. Each difference is kept or dismissed, fresh every run. Kept changes go in through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. A Done task ticks its box only on yes. A new child is added as a task, with its id recorded in `work-item.md`, only on yes. It never writes a field to Azure Boards. A reply comment is stripped and posted only on yes. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-ado-sync` (Pull spec changes) may run from any lane. It reads the Features whose ids are recorded in `work-item.md` files and the landscape table, or only the ids the user names. It shows what differs from the spec or is new. It reads the checks from Acceptance Criteria when the Feature type has that field, and from the Acceptance checks list in the Description when it does not, so a match is not a change. Discussion comments use an api version current `az` can parse (`7.1-preview`). A missing id stays missing. The user keeps or dismisses each change. Dismissals start fresh each run. A kept change goes to the spec through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. A no-spec-yet Feature names a starter such as `/crav1-spark-to-spec` and does not run it. A reply comment is posted only after the user says yes, and only when the spec already answers the question. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start those lanes. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. The six starter options stay unchanged. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-run-exploratory-test` may run from any lane, after a build of a slice already exists. Pass one learns the slice by using it once. Pass two is no longer careful. It adds randomness and follows what the last action showed. It lasts about as long as the first pass, long enough to provoke bugs, then it stops. That stop is named `matched the first pass`. It stops sooner when the user says stop. That stop is named `the user said stop`. The user does not set a clock. It writes bugs to `docs/specs/<slug>/explore.md`. It does not write the checks the plan already named. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not start those lanes. A bug it finds is not sent to `/crav1-fix-bug` unless the user says so in that turn. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

`/crav1-suggest-tests-for-code` may run from any lane. The user points at code that already exists, one repo or one area, not the whole system. It reads that code and suggests tests for what that code can actually break. A function gets a few checks. A page gets a browser check. A boundary gets an integration check. It does not dump every test type. Every suggestion stays listed. Nothing is dropped to keep the list short. The user answers them in one batch: keep, leave, or dismiss (a single yes takes the recommendations). Dismiss means it is not offered again. A kept suggestion goes onto the existing spec through `/crav1-add-to-spec`. Plan turns it into a task. It does not write the tests, change the code, or start Specify, Plan, or Build. It does not move work into a lane. It is a later skill. It is not one of the six starter options. When the user asks for startup options, that ask names the six and does not run this skill. The six starter options stay unchanged. Spark, specify, plan, and verify do not run it.

Research is a cross-cutting helper with no slash command. Flag it when a run hits a technical question that needs research before Specify or Plan can proceed: choosing a technology or service, changing the architecture, scaling or modernizing, or judging an idea nobody has built yet.

Any lane that hits this flags it to the process orchestrator or guild lead, who pauses that lane and sends the researcher the question, the product or feature slug, and any constraints.

The researcher treats the project's existing specs, plans, and code as the current state. For parts those do not cover, the researcher may use `/crav1-existing-to-specs`. Running that command is the skill writing the architecture spec, and the system notes when those notes are not already there. The researcher does not hand-edit those files.

The full study lives wherever the team keeps its research. The researcher writes a short note under `docs/research/` (for example `docs/research/<topic>.md`) with the recommendation, trade-offs, confidence, and a link to the full study, and adds a line under `## Research findings` on the spec that names that path. The kit's skills read `docs/research/` and `## Research findings`. No skill reads a `research.md` inside a spec folder. The researcher returns the recommendation to the process orchestrator or guild lead with a suggested lane. That role routes it.

Aside from that note and that Research findings line, the researcher does not edit specs, plans, or code, and does not change the lane.

When a note in `docs/research/` is updated, the skill that writes it follows the clear check in [`.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/research-stale-clear.md`](../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/references/research-stale-clear.md). So do `/crav1-add-to-spec` and `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` when the user points that command at the file. The kit checks each listed point. It does not ask the user. An older mark with no point lines is split into the hits it was made from. The note's own open questions are routed when the answer lies outside the note's owner, including when the mark clears. It clears the mark when every point is resolved, and otherwise narrows it and routes each open point. `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` re-checks a point when the open question it was waiting on is answered. The mark clears when no point is open. It does not commit.

## Maintainer note

This page is generated (1.107.0). Lanes come from each skill's and subagent's `lane`, and the text from the `routing` block, in [`docs/reference/skills.yaml`](reference/skills.yaml). Edit that file, then run `python3 scripts/gen-skill-docs.py`; CI fails when this page is stale. Notify your process orchestrator or guild lead, if you have one, with the routing diff.

## Recommended option

Every question with options that has a recommendation lists that option first and ends its label with ` (Recommended)`. The question text does not also say `Recommendation: X`. This covers the opening questions of `/crav1-build-tasks`, `/crav1-fix-build-gaps`, `/crav1-add-to-spec`, `/crav1-ado-sync`, `/crav1-existing-to-specs`, `/crav1-finalize-commit`, and `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` (marked only when the message or files make one option the better fit), keep, leave, dismiss, or note in `/crav1-add-to-spec`, keep or redact and the image options in the imported-sources check, the suggested patch letter in `/crav1-tighten-spec` and `/crav1-tighten-plan`, the branch choice in `/crav1-create-feature-branch`, and the task type in `/crav1-ado-sync`. The shared rule is in `crav1.mdc` (and `CLAUDE.md`).

## Choice words for bots and scripted runs

The merged skills take exact choice words instead of `--flags`. A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking, for a person, a bot, or a headless run. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words; it does not guess. Runners should always pass the word.

| Skill | Question | Words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | What to read | `repos only` · `repos and bundle` |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | What to write | `one spec` · `spec per feature` |
| `/crav1-existing-to-specs` | Recheck existing specs (1.108.0) | `recheck` · `repos vs specs` |
| `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` | List (optional, never asked) | `detailed` |
| `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` | Show or ask | `show` · `ask` |
| `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions` | Channel after ask (optional) | `research` |
| `/crav1-add-to-spec` | What you have | `fact` · `dump` · `code change` · `meeting` · `mail` · `chat` |
| `/crav1-build-tasks` | Which tasks | `one task` · `range` · `all tasks` |
| `/crav1-build-tasks` | Branch | `new branch` |
| `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` | Which gaps | `verify gaps` · `live gaps` |
| `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` | Branch | `new branch` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Commit or message | `commit` · `message only` · `commit now` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Base branch | `new branch` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Pull | `pull` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Style | `crav1` · `git log` |
| `/crav1-finalize-commit` | Trailer hook | `strip trailers` · `keep trailers` |
| `/crav1-review-pr` | Review a branch (optional, 1.80.0) | `branch` |
| `/crav1-review-pr` | PR branches on disk older than the pull request | `fetch pr branches` · `use disk` · `stop pr review` |
| `/crav1-review-pr` | The comment as posted | `comment posted` · `newest comment` · `skip comment record` |
| `/crav1-pr-status` | Which pull request | `pr<n>` |
| `/crav1-pr-status` | Your side (optional; picked from the PR author otherwise) | `as reviewer` · `as author` |
| `/crav1-pr-status` | How much | `since last` · `no code` |
| `/crav1-merge-pr` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-merge-pr` | The PR record says not ready (1.97.0) | `anyway` |
| `/crav1-help` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-help` | What to do next (optional, never asked) | `todo` · `todo next` · `todo top N` |
| `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` | Also check the latest pipeline runs? | `pipeline runs` |
| `/crav1-explain-this-code` | How deep | `what it does` · `what and why` · `teach the language` |
| `/crav1-retire-spec` | What to do | `retire` · `merge` · `park` · `convert to note` |
| `/crav1-glossary` | Which mode | `as-file` · `research` · `<term>` |
| `/crav1-ado-sync` | Which sync | `suggest features` · `push features` · `push tasks` · `pull tasks` · `pull spec changes` |

Example: `/crav1-ado-sync push tasks`, `/crav1-existing-to-specs repos and bundle spec per feature`.
